title: ICICI Bank, SBI: Foreign brokerages pick winners in the Indian banking pack
text:
Bernstein and Goldman Sachs have turned bullish on select Indian banks, projecting a broad-based earnings recovery over the next few years. In recent sector reports, the two foreign brokerages pointed to healthy loan growth, improving funding conditions, stable or higher net interest margins (NIMs), asset quality, and continued cost discipline.

Bernstein expects sector loan growth of 13-15 per cent in FY27, driven by higher inflation and stronger nominal credit. Liquidity conditions should continue to support credit expansion, although any policy tightening to contain rising inflation could moderate growth momentum later this year, it said. The brokerage expects net interest margins (NIMs) to remain stable, with the bulk of deposit repricing now behind banks.

“Any upward movement in policy rates, however, could provide a near-term tailwind to margins. Asset quality is also expected to remain benign, with no signs of meaningful deterioration in system-wide stress indicators,” said Pranav Gundlapalle, Ishan Mittal and Anirudh Gupta of Bernstein in a recent report.

Earnings recovery

Goldman Sachs analysts are also positive about the banking sector, arguing that the macroeconomic backdrop is approaching an inflexion point. The brokerage’s GS Macro Lead Indicator says the environment is favourable for banks, provided geopolitical conditions do not deteriorate.

Goldman Sachs expects core pre-provision operating profit (PPoP) growth to rise to the high teens during FY27-FY29, driving strong stock returns.

Its conviction on an earnings recovery is based on factors such as stronger loan growth led by a recovery in retail lending, sustained momentum in the micro, small and medium enterprise segment, and an improving deposit-growth outlook.

Goldman Sachs expects deposit growth across banks to benefit from robust mobilisation of Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank). It also sees scope for NIM improvement, driven by a more favourable funding environment, a shift towards higher-margin loans, and the possibility of higher interest rates in calendar 2028.

Asset-quality trends should also support earnings. The brokerage expects unsecured loan performance to improve further, while continued cost discipline — driven by income growth outpacing operating expenses — will aid overall bank margins over the next two years.

Preferred picks

Among large private banks, Goldman Sachs sees the strongest upside in ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank, supported by expected core PPoP growth of 17 per cent and 15 per cent, respectively, over FY26-FY29. It has initiated coverage on HDFC Bank and Axis Bank with a “buy” rating, despite expecting further downward revisions to consensus earnings estimates, citing attractive valuations.

Bernstein rates ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, HDFC Bank and IndusInd Bank as “outperform”, while Kotak Mahindra Bank and State Bank of India (SBI) are tagged “market-perform”. The brokerage has updated its models for Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and SBI following the lenders’ latest quarterly results, making modest changes to its assumptions on growth and margins.

Goldman Sachs believes that any further re-rating for mid-sized banks will require sustained return on equity above the cost of equity — a challenging ask for several such lenders. It has given IDFC First Bank, Bandhan Bank and IndusInd Bank “neutral” ratings, while Yes Bank and RBL Bank have been rated “sell”.

AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank have been initiated with “buy” ratings. Federal Bank, meanwhile, is viewed as a turnaround story as it continues its transformation.

Goldman Sachs is cautious about public-sector banks. It expects gradual normalisation of credit costs and structurally lower core PPoP margins to weigh on return on assets. It has initiated Bank of Baroda and Punjab National Bank with “sell” ratings. SBI has been rated “neutral”, supported by its stronger funding franchise and improving fee-income profile.
